title: Localization decomposition of a finite module with finite maximal support
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $M$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $\mathfrak m_1,\ldots,\mathfrak m_r$ be distinct maximal ideals and suppose that $M_{\mathfrak q}=0$ for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ other than the listed ideals, where localization is [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then the canonical $R$-linear map
$$M\longrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^r M_{\mathfrak m_i},\qquad m\longmapsto(m/1)_i,$$
is an isomorphism. The list may include ideals at which $M$ is zero. If $r=0$, the assertion says that $M=0$.

source.place: Tag 00L2, lemma-support-closed, applied to R/Ann(M), followed by Tag 00JA, lemma-product-local, or Tag 00JB, lemma-artinian-finite-length: tensor the finite product decomposition of R/Ann(M) with M.

proof.text: Put $I=\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)$ and $B=R/I$, acting on $M$ by $\bar a m=am$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator], the primes containing $I$ are precisely the primes at which $M$ is nonzero. Thus they are exactly the $\mathfrak m_i$ with $i\in J:=\{i:I\subseteq\mathfrak m_i\}$. Primes of $B$ correspond to primes of $R$ containing $I$: inverse image under $R\to B$ preserves the proper-ideal and prime-product conditions, and the inverse sends $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$ to $\mathfrak p/I$, with quotient $B/(\mathfrak p/I)=R/\mathfrak p$. Consequently every prime of $B$ is one of the distinct maximal ideals $\mathfrak n_i=\mathfrak m_i/I$ for $i\in J$.

source.place: Tag 00L2, lemma-support-closed; quotient ideal correspondence written out

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] to the zero ideal of $B$. It gives $\sqrt{(0)}=\bigcap_{i\in J}\mathfrak n_i$. Hence each element of this intersection is nilpotent. If $J$ is empty, the intersection is $B$, so $1$ is nilpotent, $B=0$, and $M=0$ because $1_B$ acts as the identity. In that case every localization of $M$ is zero and the conclusion follows, including the empty list. Henceforth suppose $J\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology, (7), for I=0; zero module localization from fractions

proof.text: Now [lem-weil-pbc-product-of-localizations-at-maximal] applies to $B$: its maximal ideals are exactly the finite list $(\mathfrak n_i)_{i\in J}$ and their intersection consists of nilpotent elements. Write its canonical ring isomorphism as $\theta:B\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i\in J}B_{\mathfrak n_i}$. Let $e_i\in B$ be the inverse image of the tuple with $1$ in position $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. Componentwise multiplication and addition give $e_i^2=e_i$, $e_ie_j=0$ for $i\ne j$, and $\sum_i e_i=1$.

Write $e_iM=\{e_im:m\in M\}$. The $R$-linear maps $M\to\prod_{i\in J}e_iM$, $m\mapsto(e_im)_i$, and $(x_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i x_i$ are inverse: their composites are $\sum_i e_im=m$ and $(\sum_j e_ix_j)_i=(x_i)_i$, since $x_j=e_jx_j$. This is a finite sum, so there is no direct-product/direct-sum issue.

proof.text: Compose the isomorphism in step 4 with the product of the $\phi_i$. Its $i$th component is $(e_im)/1=m/1$, so it is the required canonical map on the indices in $J$. If $i\notin J$, choose $a\in I\setminus\mathfrak m_i$. Then $am=0$ for all $m$, while $a$ acts invertibly on $M_{\mathfrak m_i}$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; thus $M_{\mathfrak m_i}=0$. Inserting these zero factors is an isomorphism, with inverse the coordinate projection to $J$, and gives exactly the claimed map for the whole listed set.
